subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Yesterday, / my surgeon / operate on my knee.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence has a verb tense issue in the phrase "**operate on my knee**".
 
• Since the action "operate" is in the past, it should be in the **past tense** form "operated".
 
• Thus, the corrected phrase should be "**operated on my knee**".
 
• Other parts of the sentence are correct: 
 
 
• **Yesterday** – correct usage, indicating the past.
 
• **My surgeon** – grammatically correct subject.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Yesterday, my surgeon **operated** on my knee."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Operate** is the **present tense** form, so it should be changed to the past tense "operated" when referring to a completed action.
 
• The correct construction for a past action is the use of the past form of the verb: "**operated**".
